bugs.summary: `writeChar()` on Windows counts supplementary characters twice

comments.text:
## Summary

`do_writechar()` counts the characters of each element with
`mbstowcs(NULL, s, 0)`.  Where `wchar_t` is 16-bit (Windows), `mbstowcs()`
returns the number of UTF-16 code units, so each supplementary ("non-BMP")
character such as `"\U0001F600"` counts as 2.  `nchars` therefore means
something different on Windows than on other platforms -- and something
different from what `readChar()` and `nchar()` mean by a "char" on Windows
itself.  `?writeChar` describes `nchars` as a number of characters, with no
platform qualification.

This surfaced as a Windows check failure of the regression test added with
the PR#19112 fix in r90334: the test writes 100 supplementary characters with
`nchars = 399L` and expects a 699-byte file; Windows writes 599 bytes.

## Reproducible example

Run on Windows, in a UTF-8 locale:

```
su <- strrep("\U0001F600", 100L)   # 100 characters, 400 bytes in UTF-8
nchar(su, "chars")
## [1] 100                <- R counts code points itself, also on Windows

tf <- tempfile(); f <- file(tf, "wb")
suppressWarnings(writeChar(su, f, nchars = 399L, eos = NULL))
close(f)
file.size(tf)
## Unix, macOS: 699       (400 bytes + 299 padding: 399 - 100 characters)
## Windows:     599       (400 bytes + 199 padding: 399 - 200 UTF-16 units)
```

This is part (c) of the PR#19112 regression test in `tests/reg-encodings.R`,
whose unconditional `stopifnot(all.equal(file.size(tf), 699))` currently
fails on Windows.

## Analysis

Both the buffer-sizing loop and the writing loop of `do_writechar()` count
characters the same way (`src/main/connections.c:5419-5420` and `:5506`):

```
	    size_t nb = strlen(ss),
		nc = mbcslocale ? mbstowcs(NULL, ss, 0) : nb;
```

With a 16-bit `wchar_t`, converting a supplementary character yields a UTF-16
surrogate pair, so `mbstowcs(NULL, s, 0)` counts it twice.  The padding
arithmetic `nb += tt - nc` then under-pads by one byte per supplementary
character.

`readChar()` never goes through `wchar_t`: in a UTF-8 locale,
`readFixedString()` and `rawFixedString()` walk the input with `utf8clen()`,
one character at a time (`connections.c:5189-5212`, `:5245-5259`), and
`nchar(x, "chars")` likewise counts code points.  So on Windows,
`writeChar(x, con, nchars = n)` and `readChar(con, nchars = n)` disagree
about what a "char" is whenever `x` contains supplementary characters.

The truncation branch (`nchars` smaller than the character count,
`connections.c:5423-5433` and the matching loop in the writer) compares
`tt < nc` against the same inflated count before consuming characters with
`Mbrtowc()`; for non-BMP input this path was exercised by no test on any
platform.

## Candidate patch

Add `mbCharCount()` and `mbBytesForChars()` helpers used by both the
buffer-sizing loop and the writing loop: in a UTF-8 locale, count complete
UTF-8 characters directly via `utf8clen()` -- the same idiom `readChar()`
uses -- and in other MBCS locales keep the existing `mbstowcs()`/`Mbrtowc()`
code (those encodings have no supplementary-plane characters, so the counts
agree).

```
/* Number of characters in 's': where wchar_t is 16-bit (Windows),
   mbstowcs() returns the number of UTF-16 code units, counting each
   supplementary ("non-BMP") character twice, so in a UTF-8 locale count
   complete UTF-8 characters directly, as readChar() and nchar() do.
   Returns (size_t)-1 for an invalid multibyte string. */
static size_t mbCharCount(const char *s)
{
    size_t nc = mbstowcs(NULL, s, 0);

    if(utf8locale && (int) nc >= 0) {
	nc = 0;
	for(const char *p = s; *p; p += utf8clen(*p))
	    nc++;
    }
    return nc;
}

/* Byte length of the first 'nchars' characters of 's'.  For an invalid
   multibyte string (valid = FALSE), Mbrtowc() signals an error when it
   reaches the first invalid sequence. */
static size_t mbBytesForChars(const char *s, R_xlen_t nchars, Rboolean valid)
{
    const char *p = s;

    if(valid && utf8locale) {
	for(R_xlen_t j = 0; j < nchars && *p; j++)
	    p += utf8clen(*p);
    } else {
	mbstate_t mb_st;
	mbs_init(&mb_st);
	for(R_xlen_t j = 0; j < nchars; j++) {
	    size_t used = Mbrtowc(NULL, p, R_MB_CUR_MAX, &mb_st);
	    if(!used) break;
	    p += used;
	}
    }
    return (size_t)(p - s);
}
```

Properties:

- On platforms with 32-bit `wchar_t` (Unix, macOS), behavior is unchanged:
  for valid strings, the `utf8clen()` walk returns exactly what
  `mbstowcs()`/`Mbrtowc()` returned.
- Invalid multibyte strings take the previous `Mbrtowc()` path unchanged
  (`mbCharCount()` still calls `mbstowcs()` first, so invalidity is still
  detected), preserving the existing "invalid multibyte string at ..."
  error behavior.
- On Windows, `nchars` now counts supplementary characters once,
  consistently with `readChar()` and `nchar()`, and the unconditional
  `file.size(tf) == 699` expectation in `tests/reg-encodings.R` holds on
  Windows too.

The patch also adds a truncation test (`nchars` smaller than the number of
characters) with supplementary characters.  Its assertions deliberately use
`readBin()`/raw comparisons rather than `readChar()`: whether UCRT's
`mbrtowc()` (used in `readFixedString()`'s per-character validity check)
accepts 4-byte UTF-8 sequences with a 16-bit `wchar_t` is a separate open
question, and `readChar()` of non-BMP text on Windows deserves its own
test and investigation.

## Compatibility

This changes what Windows writes for the (rare) case
`nchars != number of characters` with non-BMP input: previously-written
padded files effectively used UTF-16-unit counts.  Given that the
padding/truncation path for non-BMP characters was inconsistent between
`writeChar()` and `readChar()` and untested, treating the old Windows
behavior as a bug seems right, but that is R-core's call.  The alternative
is to keep the Windows behavior, special-case the r90334 regression test
(`if(onWindows) 599`, proposed as
<https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/280>), and document that on Windows
`nchars` counts UTF-16 code units.

## Verification after patching

On all platforms, including Windows:

```
su <- strrep("\U0001F600", 100L)

## (c) of the PR#19112 regression test: padding
tf <- tempfile(); f <- file(tf, "wb")
suppressWarnings(writeChar(su, f, nchars = 399L, eos = NULL))
close(f)
stopifnot(file.size(tf) == 699)

## truncation, previously untested for non-BMP input on any platform
r2 <- writeChar(su, raw(), nchars = 50L, eos = NULL)
tf2 <- tempfile(); f <- file(tf2, "wb")
writeChar(su, f, nchars = 50L, eos = NULL)
close(f)
stopifnot(exprs = {
    identical(r2, charToRaw(strrep("\U0001F600", 50L)))
    file.size(tf2) == 200
    identical(readBin(tf2, "raw", 300L), charToRaw(strrep("\U0001F600", 50L)))
})
```

Both checks are included in the patch as additions to
`tests/reg-encodings.R`, and pass in the r-svn mirror's CI on Linux, macOS,
and both Windows runners (x86_64 and aarch64).
